properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 5 at 1:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
At 100 PM AST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
La Alianza, or near Florida, moving northwest at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and frequent lightning. Funnel
clouds are possible.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to outdoor objects is possible. Gusty winds
could knock down tree limbs and blow around unsecured
objects.

Locations impacted include...
Arecibo, Hatillo, Camuy, Florida, Barceloneta, Quebradillas,
Bajadero, Rafael Capo, Rafael Gonzalez, La Alianza, Imbery,
Pajonal, Corcovado, Animas, Carrizales, Sabana Hoyos and Quebrada.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 5 at 12:43PM EDT until October 5 at 3:45PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Calhoun County in the panhandle of Florida...
Southeastern Jackson County in the panhandle of Florida...

* Until 245 PM CDT.

* At 1143 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2.5 and 3.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Grand Ridge, Altha, Willis, Chason, White Pond, Sink Creek, Union
City, Chipola, Alliance, Camps Head, Henderson Mill, Simsville,
Moose Pond, Center Lake, Ocheesee and Cypress.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 5 at 12:35PM EDT until October 8 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents expected.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM Tuesday to 5
AM EDT Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from Tuesday
morning through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with maximum temperatures in the mid-90s to

* WHERE...The East Bay and San Francisco Bay Shoreline, North Bay

Hills, The Santa Cruz Mountains, Interior Monterey County and the
Santa Lucia Range, Most of San Benito County and the Cholame Hills

Seco and Lake San Antonio.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects anyone without effective
cooling and/or adequate hydration. Impacts likely in some health
systems, heat-sensitive industries and infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

Beat the heat and check the backseat! Do not leave young children or
pets in unattended vehicles. Car interiors will reach lethal
temperatures in a matter of minutes.
